Messages.Author: Oko
Messages.Body:
Minion A (acting) plays Disarm on minion B.

The question is; Is there a window of opportunity to burn 3 blood for
Disarm, before A play's Amaranth?

Messages.Author: Eric Simon
Messages.Body:
"Oko" <o...@vedatassuus.com> wrote in message news:<c1ldtl$l7s$1...@phys-news1.kolumbus.fi>...

> Minion A (acting) plays Disarm on minion B.
>
> The question is; Is there a window of opportunity to burn 3 blood for
> Disarm, before A play's Amaranth?

IANLSJ, but I don't see why not. The problem is, that doesn't help
you avoid the Amaranth. Minion B no longer "has" the card, so is no
longer at -1/-2 strength, but that doesn't cancel the "go to torpor"
effect. Take a look at the text:

Disarm
Combat
pot
Only usable at the end of a round of combat in which this vampire
successfully inflicted more damage at close range than the opposing
vampire; not usable by a vampire going into torpor. Put this card on
the opposing vampire and send that vampire into torpor. The vampire
with this card has -1 strength; he or she may burn this card by
burning 3 blood. A vampire can only have 1 Disarm.

POT
As above, but the vampire with this card has -2 strength.

Note that there are two things happening:
1) Put this card on the opposing vampire
2) Send that vampire to torpor

Getting rid of 1) does not get rid of 2). Minion B is still going to
torpor, with or without the Disarm, allowing Amaranth to be played.
It's a nice thought, but doesn't quite work as one might like it to.

Eric Simon
Prince of Chicago

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


No. A gets first chance to play the next effect, per 1.6.1.6.

If B was acting, then yes.

As already noted, the result would only be a decrease in the amount
of blood to be gained inthe diablerie - the vampire would still be
on his way to torpor, an elligible target for Amaranth.
